full_name: Camiral Golf & Wellness, Tour Course (formerly PGA Catalunya Resort)

summary.text: The Tour Course at Camiral Golf & Wellness, formerly PGA Catalunya, is the resort's shorter, more open and less demanding second 18, designed by Neil Coles and Angel Gallardo.

setting.text: Top100golfcourses describes pine tree-lined fairways with strategically placed bunkers and cunningly positioned water hazards.
The club calls it equally beautiful as the Stadium Course but shorter and less daunting, with wide fairways that tolerate imperfect shots while water hazards punish the unwary.
Where2golf puts the Tour Course at about 6,000 metres from the back tees, par 72.

history.text: The Tour Course opened in 2005, joining the older Stadium Course.
It was designed by Neil Coles and Angel Gallardo, then chairman and vice chairman of the European Tour, the same pair as the Stadium.
The European Tour Qualifying School Final Stage has been co-hosted at the resort on seven occasions since 2008.
Top100golfcourses says professionals tee it up on the Tour Course every winter during Final Qualifying School and that it demands respect even from them.
The resort rebranded from PGA Catalunya to Camiral Golf & Wellness in December 2022.

trivia.text: Top100golfcourses calls it a fine track in its own right, though it says the Stadium Course completely overshadows it.
Camiral has been confirmed as host of the 2031 Ryder Cup, which will be played on the Stadium Course rather than the Tour Course.

2.text: A par three listed at 180 metres, a precise mid-iron framed by tall trees, so the wind may be hard to feel or see.

3.text: A par four listed at 333 metres where bunkers lurk down the right and the green sits at an angle over water.

5.text: A par five listed at 466 metres, reachable in two despite awkward cross bunkers. The club says its green is by far the most sloping on the course.

7.text: A par five listed at 509 metres with two routes: follow the dogleg, or cut the corner over a copse of trees on the right.

8.text: A par three listed at 168 metres that the club calls probably the most difficult short hole on the course, with deep bunkers.

14.text: An unusual par three listed at 185 metres with no sand bunkers, only four grassy hollows that catch short shots.

15.text: A par five listed at 459 metres that the club advises playing as a genuine three-shot hole, laying up short of a ditch.

16.text: A par three listed at 129 metres that the club calls a definite birdie hole, with a generous green behind three bunkers.

18.text: A par five listed at 475 metres, with the fairway rippling between sand to a well-guarded green and two cleverly placed fairway bunkers.

local.text: The resort is outside Caldes de Malavella, about 45 minutes north of Barcelona and a few kilometres from Girona airport.
Where2golf places it about 15 km south of Girona.
